# dsh-focus-board
A cross-session task ledger for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`).
Long conversations lose the original intent, several requests inside one conversation blur into each
other, and conclusions reached halfway get quietly overtaken by later code. A memory plugin retriev

es
text; it does not hold an authoritative list of *what is still open and what the next step is*.

This plugin owns that list. It is a plain JSON ledger on disk, a `focus` tool the agent writes
throu
gh, and a strip above the composer that the human reads — both of you looking at the same rows.
English | 中文
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Restart `dsh web` (or refresh the page if only the client half changed). The entry appears in the
gl
obal sidebar as **焦点台 / Focus Board**.
## What you get

- **One item per request.** `focus open` on every new request, `focus update` while working,
`focus

close` with a conclusion. Items carry a step chain (`plan`), notes, links, stall owner,
and artifact

s, so the panel can draw the flow instead of a bare sentence.
- **A strip above the composer.** Coll

apsed to titles, one expanded at a time, width following the
composer. It shows only the current con

versation's items, plus a quiet announcement band at the
top of the window while the plugin is worki

ng.
- **Injected context.** Unfinished items are injected into every step, so a fresh turn still kno

ws
what is open. A `docs/项目大纲.md` (or `AI_GUARD.md`) outline is injected next to it and is
preferred

over guessing when a choice comes up.
- **Staleness review.** Code and docs move; a conclusion writ

ten a week ago may already be wrong.
Each item carries a review clock and fingerprints of its artifa

cts (`⟳ stale Nd`, `⚠ basis
changed`, `⚠ basis missing`), so the board tells you what to re-check in

stead of trusting it.
- **Choices that learn.** `kind: 'choice'` with options renders as clickable c

andidates; the ledger
remembers what was picked, and `focus auto` decides safe repeat cases on its o

wn. Dangerous
actions (push, deploy, delete, tag, spend) are never auto-decided.
- **A grant ledger

(`grant`).** Local capability questions — push? deploy? write to production? —
are answered from a t

able instead of being re-asked. Each entry has four modes (always / timed /
ask / never), an optiona

l scope, and a pointer to *where the credential lives* (never the value).
Items blocked on authoriza

tion render that same four-mode control **inside the item card**; if the
entry does not exist yet it

is created first, so the panel and the ledger never disagree.
- **Blind-work backfill.** When only

a human can do the step and the result is invisible to the
agent (a console toggle, a token revocati

on), the item asks for a 3–5 point self-check instead of
accepting "done".
- **Answer-driven re-judg

e.** The scheduler does not react to "the conversation changed" — that
[该节后续省略]
## Tools
| Tool | Purpose |
| `focus` | `open` / `update` / `close` / `drop` / `list` / `review` / `decide` / `auto` / `brief` |
| `grant` | `list` / `check` / `upsert` / `remove` — answers "may I do this class of action?" |

`grant` stores *where* a credential lives (`env:NAME`, `file:/path#KEY`, `conv:SESSION`, `mem:ID`,
`
keychain:NAME`), never the value itself: the ledger is injected into every prompt.

## Optional integrations

Two sub-boards talk to a specific machine layout. Both are disabled until configured; the ledger,
st
rip, scheduler and grants work without them.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The same values can come from environment variables: `DSH_FOCUS_OWNER`, `DSH_FOCUS_ARRAY_ROOT`,
`DSH
_FOCUS_GITEE_ENGINE`, `OPSCTL_PYTHON`, `DSH_FOCUS_DEPLOY_REGISTRY`.
The deploy sub-board runs SSH commands defined by *your* registry (checkout a tag, sync an env file,
install, restart, health-check). It is a convenience for one machine, not a general CI system; the
authorization table gates it like everything else.
## Status & known rough edges
Early software (0.x). It has been used daily for real work, but expect rough edges: the UI is dense,
some copy is Chinese-only, and the optional integrations assume a Unix-ish remote host. Issues and

inese-only, and the optional integrations assume a Unix-ish remote host. Issues and
PRs are welcome.
### One action per card, and cards that are busy get out of your way

Every card in the focus sub-board carries several buttons that either write the ledger or send a
pro

mpt (decide / backfill / close / park / review / re-judge / send / loop). Pressing one of them
locks

the whole card for the round trip: the other buttons are disabled, the card cannot be expanded,
the

header says which action is running and why the rest are locked. The lock is kept in a
synchronous

`Map`, so a double click cannot slip through; it clears when the write returns (20 s
timeout unlocks

and asks you to refresh to see whether the ledger landed), and checkboxes, evidence
inputs, prompt
drafts and inline grant controls lock with it.

A card that is currently being advanced — a write in flight, the loop pinned to it, a re-judge in
fl

ight, or the host reporting its session moved within 5 minutes (`item.live`) — is rendered
**dimmed,

desaturated, auto-collapsed and not expandable**, with a spinning micro-icon and a line
saying it w

ill reopen by itself. Cards waiting on you are exempt: they stay readable and expandable
even if the
ir session just moved.
Test: `node test/ui-lock.mjs` (26 assertions, stubbed renderer, no host, no real ledger).
## Security

Installing a DSH plugin runs third-party code with your own permissions. This one can, **if you
conf

igure it**, run git and SSH commands and read a credentials file you create. It never sends data
any

where and never stores a secret value in the ledger. Read the source before you install; the whole
p
lugin is two files (`index.js`, `client.js`).
